abstract: Japan Broadcasting Corporation is shifting to file-based systems for its television production and playout systems, including videotape recorders and editing machines. A variety of codecs and formats based on the material exchange format for broadcast equipment have been adopted. These include Motion Picture Experts Group 2 (MPEG-2) or advanced video coding and operational pattern 1a or atom. Video files need to be converted into the selected codec and format to operate efficiently. The quality of video and audio must be checked during this conversion process, because degradation and noise may occur. This paper describes equipment that can quickly convert files to multiple formats, as well as intelligently check the quality of video and audio during the conversion. The equipment automatically adjusts thresholds to detect anomalies in the video quality check, depending on the type of codec and the spatial frequency of each area. This can be done in less time than the actual video duration by optimizing the processing software.

authors.bio: Kenichiro Ichikawa received B.S. and M.S. degrees from the Keio University in 2002 and 2004, respectively. Following graduation, he joined Japan Broadcasting Corp. (NHK) and built his career as a video engineer through studio program production and live telecasts. He is currently involved in the development of new broadcasting systems, particularly video and master control systems. Ichikawa is currently an engineer at NHK's Program Engineering division.
authors.name: Kenichiro Ichikawa

authors.bio: Takuji Shimmi received B.S. and M.S. degrees from Waseda University in 1990 and 1992, respectively. Following graduation, he joined NHK and built his career as a video engineer through studio program production and live telecasts. Shimmi was involved in the development of new broadcasting systems, particularly editing and file-based systems. He currently works as a senior engineer in the Planning and General Affairs division at NHK.
authors.name: Takuji Shimmi

authors.bio: Kentaro Higashijima received B.S. and M.S. degrees from Keio University in 1999 and 2001, respectively. Following graduation, he joined NHK and built his career as a video engineer through studio program production and live telecasts. Higashijima was involved in the development of new broadcasting systems, particularly camera, video and ob-van systems. He currently works as a principal engineer in the planning division at NHK.
authors.name: Kentaro Higashijima

authors.bio: Yasunori Iguchi received an M.S. degree from Nara Institute of Science and Technology in 2001. Following graduation, he joined NHK and built his career as a video engineer through video editing and studio program production. Iguchi was involved in the development of new broadcasting systems, particularly file-based production systems. He is currently an engineer in NHK's Program Engineering division.
authors.name: Yasunori Iguchi
